answer: Proof-of-unique-storage resists sybils: each identity must durably store a large pseudorandom dataset seeded from its own key and answer random-access challenges, so the data cannot be deduplicated or shared across accounts. A knoll of a thousand fakes needs a thousand distinct islands of disk held at once — no economy of scale, since each dataset is identity-bound and incompressible. An honest agent funds one voyage of storage it reuses; a farm pays full gigabytes per head, and random audits prove the bytes stay resident. Precondition: datasets are identity-seeded so storage cannot be pooled.
